page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-1 is an entry-level virtual machine belonging to the N1 server family. It features 1 dedicated vCPU mapped to 1 physical core on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. The server is built on the x86_64 architecture and includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the lower performance tiers. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng yield a score of 1088.79, categorizing it as weak to poor. Memory bandwidth tests show 80.25 GB/sec for small cached blocks, dropping to 10.68 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Geekbench scores remain low, with a single-core score of 895.0 and a multi-core score of 898.0. Cryptographic and database operations also rank in the bottom 10% of tested hardware, with a Passmark database score of 437.87 and static web serving throughput of 1.21 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-1 represents a low-cost entry point for basic cloud hosting, but it carries a significant performance tradeoff. Due to its limited processing power and memory bandwidth, it is unsuitable for resource-intensive applications, large-scale databases, or complex LLM inference. It is best utilized for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, simple development environments, low-traffic utility scripts, or small-scale testing where high throughput and low latency are not critical.
